Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned Addl. Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 438, Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Section 420, 468, 471, 200, 109 of I.P.C. in C.T. Case No.577 of 2019 of the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Athagarh arising out of Khuntuni P.S. Case No.171 of 2019.
4.
It is stated by learned counsel for the Petitioner that initially the present case arises out of land dispute between the Petitioner and the complainant group.
He further contended that initially the Petitioner was issued with a notice under Section 35 of B.N.S.S.
He further submitted that due to some personal difficulty, the Petitioner could not appear.
As a result of which the Petitioner is apprehending his arrest in the hands of the local police.
He further submitted that although the case is of the year 2019, however, no final charge sheet has been filed as of now.

5. Considering the seriousness of the allegation, gravity of the offence and the facts of the case,
although I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner, however it is observed that, in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail before the learned court in seisin over the matter within a period of three weeks from today, he shall be released on bail on such terms and Jayadev Jena vs State Of Odisha .....

6. Release of the Petitioner shall be subject to a condition that:-
I) initially the Petitioner was issued a notice under Section 35 of B.N.S.S.; and II) the Petitioner does not have any similar criminal antecedent.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of the bail.
7. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
